subject: fennec
reasoning:
I'm planning out the fennec fox proportions and skeleton structure, sizing the body, oversized ears, and spine chain from hips through chest to head so the model stays anatomically believable.

Now I'm working through the exact joint coordinates and naming scheme for the spine, neck, and head chains, making sure parent references connect properly down to the hips root.

For the body geometry, I'm planning sweeps along the spine and neck chains with tapering radii, using fur-toned countershaded colors for the body surface, then shaping the head as a separate sphere-based part.

Now I'm working out the snout and jaw: a tapered frustum for the upper snout attached to the head bone, and a separate jaw bone with its own frustum for the lower jaw, positioned and aimed forward and down from the head to form the muzzle shape.

I'm placing the nose as a small dark sphere at the snout tip, then adding dark spherical eyes with tiny highlight dots positioned symmetrically using local head-space coordinates, plus cream-colored cheek fur spheres. Now I'm thinking through the ears — large triangular shapes leaning outward, extruded from an outline in a plane angled away from the head.

Still working out ear geometry...

Now I'm setting up the joint naming convention for left/right ears using side labels, with outward-tilted direction vectors. Then I'm moving on to legs, planning the front leg placement from shoulder to paw using simple two-segment limbs.

Working out the hind leg chain with hip, knee, hock, and ankle joints...

Adding small cream-colored paw spheres scaled flat at the ankle joints, positioning them to sit just above the floor, then sweeping the leg chains with tapered bone radii. Now I'm starting the bushy tail as a catmull-rom curve from the hips, planning black tips.

I'll skip whiskers and eye lines but add cream muzzle/cheek markings, a dark nose, dark eyes, and tiny snout spots. For cheek fur tufts, I'm placing small spike cones near the head pointing back-and-outward to suggest a ruff.

Checking proportions: ear tip height around 0.46-0.47 against a 0.2 shoulder height feels right for a realistic fox, and the 0.17 ear length is slightly big but acceptable compared to real foxes' 0.15. Now I'm setting up the spine sweep's radius function to taper the body shape along the chain.

Planning the rump with a rounded hip sphere, and a neck sweep with tapering radius into the head sphere. For coloring I'll countershade a fur coat tone against cream, apply it broadly, and consider a cream gradient for the lower legs. Adding a small dark eye sphere positioned at the head joint, skipping a highlight dot for simplicity.

Now working out head placement: positioning the skull sphere forward from the neck joint, sizing it so it spans the right depth range, and checking that the snout, body front, and ear bases all line up proportionally without overlap.
